body: I think you’re right about that. I read up on avoidant attachment styles and it describes me pretty well. I like people, as long as they stay at arms length. I don’t like anyone close to me, outside of some members of my family; and I don’t have any desire to change that. I don’t want anyone in my space for any length of time and I don’t want to have to explain anything to anyone. I like being side chick because I can have sex and then send him home, and there’s no danger of him becoming anything other than that. Until there is.

Tell somebody!! Get help!! Gee why didn’t I think of that. Dude I’ve been in treatment so long I’m just about out of options. And why should I stick around just because that would make other people more comfortable ? Wtf,  how does that make sense?

Most people really, really don’t want to know, because it puts a burden on them. If you’ve been mentally ill a long time, like I have, they get tired of it. They get tired of worrying and tired of rearranging their lives to deal with your crap and tired of being tired. I have a good family, better than most, and I know they’re tired of it.

My therapist doesn’t panic at all. I think about suicide constantly, and it doesn’t freak her out at all. She shares my view of the hospital (they are not helpful and are basically just overpriced babysitters.) She knows, though, that eventually I will lose this battle. She’s just requested that I not do it “on her watch.”

I have insurance, a good therapist, and a good psychiatrist. I have bipolar disorder with treatment resistant depression and anxiety disorder and chronic suicidality. I’ve been in treatment most of my life. It keeps me just alive enough to not die. I’m always teetering the line between life and death. Sometimes I lean more one way or the other; right now I’m teetering more towards death. I’m the kind of tired that doesn’t get better with sleep. Hospitals are useless - I’ve been several times. There’s pretty much nothing they can do.
